_comment: Snippets are written in the syntax the compiler accepts, not in the syntax a Python editor would guess: `from "hydra" import x` is a STRING specifier, `slot` is a bare name, and loader data arrives as props. test/snippets.test.mjs checks every body against the compiler so a snippet cannot drift into an error.

Component (.hyx).description: A component: `slot` is where children land

body: # src/pages/${1:about}.hyx — this file IS the `${2:/about}` route.
Page (.hyx).description: A page: the filename is the URL, and the router passes params/path/route

Page with loader prop.description: A page whose props come from a .server.hys loader — the keys are props, not a props dict

for loop.description: A for loop in the tree; pass `key=` on the element it emits

state hook.description: Local state: `state(initial)` returns the value and its setter

Link.description: Client-side link that still renders a real href

body: button(on_click=${1:on_press}, className="rounded-lg px-4 py-2 text-sm font-semibold bg-indigo-600 text-white hover:bg-indigo-700"): ${2:label}
Button.description: A button that works with a handler prop

import from a package.description: Specifiers are STRINGS: `from hydra import x` is a parse error

export function (.hys).description: Every name another module imports needs `export`

loader (.server.hys).description: A page's server half: `hydra/server` may only be imported from a .server.hys

action (.server.hys).description: A form/mutation handler beside a loader

API route GET (.hys).description: One export per HTTP method; a dict is JSON

API middleware (.hys).description: src/middleware.hys: None passes through, anything else replies

dict comprehension.description: Comprehensions are lowered, not a library
